title: Explicit continuous unit-pivot Schur elimination
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative topological ring, let $T$ be a topological space, let $m,n\geq1$, and let $K:T\to\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(A)$ [def-weil-matrix] have entrywise continuous entries. Suppose $a(t)=K_{11}(t)$ is a unit for every $t$ and $t\mapsto a(t)^{-1}$ is continuous. Define $L_0(t)$ to be diagonal with $a(t)^{-1}$ in the $(1,1)$ position and $1$ elsewhere, define $R_0(t)$ to be the identity with $(1,j)$ entry $-a(t)^{-1}K_{1j}(t)$ for $j>1$, and define $L_1(t)$ to be the identity with $(i,1)$ entry $-a(t)^{-1}K_{i1}(t)$ for $i>1$. Put $L(t)=L_0(t)L_1(t)$ and $H_{ij}(t)=K_{ij}(t)-a(t)^{-1}K_{i1}(t)K_{1j}(t)$ for $i,j$ in the reduced index sets. Then $L$ and $R_0$ are entrywise continuous maps to $\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ and $\operatorname{GL}_m(A)$ with entrywise continuous inverses, $H$ has continuous entries, and $L(t)K(t)R_0(t)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&H(t)\end{pmatrix}$ for every $t$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite E case, pp. 18–19: continuous integral division and elementary pivot elimination; the displayed auxiliary statement is written out here because HRS uses it as a standard calculation.

proof.text: Put b=Ring.inverse(a). Define B(d,c) to have corner d, zero remaining first row, first column c below the corner, and identity reduced block. Expanding finite matrix sums with Fin.sum_univ_succ and splitting both indices with Fin.cases proves B(d,c)B(e,f)=B(de,c e+f) and B(1,0)=I. Expanding the prescribed definitions gives L=B(b,-b K_i0) and R0=B(1,-b K_0j)^T. These are computations for the entry-family matrices of def-weil-matrix.

proof.text: The unit pivot gives ba=1. Apply the B multiplication formula to obtain L B(a,K_i0)=I, since -b K_i0 a+K_i0=0 by commutativity and ba=1. Transposing the B multiplication formula gives R0 B(1,b K_0j)^T=I. IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one makes each factor a unit; it applies because square matrices over a commutative ring form a Dedekind-finite monoid. If M N=I and M is a unit, then Ring.inverse(M)=Ring.inverse(M)(M N)=N, using Ring.inverse_mul_cancel_left. Hence the actual inverses in the statement are exactly B(a,K_i0) and B(1,b K_0j)^T.

proof.text: Expanding K R0 by Fin.sum_univ_succ gives its first column K_i0 and its other entries K_ij-K_i0 b K_0j. At row zero, ab=1 makes the nonpivot entries vanish; equivalently, in the full expanded product the first row cancels using ba=1 and commutativity. The reduced entries are the prescribed H.

source.place: Agent auxiliary calculation for the continuous-pivot step; HRS Theorem 6.12(2), printed pp. 18–19, motivates continuous division but does not state this matrix identity.

proof.text: Compute all four cases of L K R0 by splitting each index into zero and successor and splitting each finite sum into the zero term and successor terms. The pivot is ba=1. Entries below it contain K_i0-b K_i0 a=0; prove this scalar cancellation first by rearranging to (1-ba)K_i0. The top row away from the pivot is zero. The remaining block is K_ij-b K_i0 K_0j: its extra term is a multiple of the already zero first-column expression. This proves exactly the prescribed block matrix identity and preserves L=L0 L1 in the given order.

source.place: Agent auxiliary calculation for the continuous-pivot step; HRS Theorem 6.12(2), printed pp. 18–19, motivates continuous division but does not state this matrix identity.

proof.text: For any continuous d:T→A and entrywise continuous c:T→(Fin s→A), B(d,c) is entrywise continuous: its four entry cases are d, zero, c_i and a constant identity entry. Apply this observation to L, R0 (with the indices transposed), and their explicit actual inverses from step 2. Their variable entries are a, b, K_i0, and ±b K_0j or ±b K_i0, continuous by hK, hinv, multiplication and negation. H is continuous by two multiplications and subtraction. This proves all five continuity clauses without global continuity of Ring.inverse.

proof.text: All computations use Fin.cases and Fin.sum_univ_succ uniformly for dimensions n+1 and m+1, so n=0 or m=0 requires no nonempty reduced index set. In the 1×1 case the block identity is ba=1. Empty T is covered because the pointwise results are universally quantified and the continuity constructions have no nonemptiness assumption. No domain, field or nontrivial-ring hypothesis is used.

I recomputed every step by hand. Step 1: N^2=0 and P^2=0, so the inverses are I-N and I-P. Step 2: L^{-1}=(I-N)D, with entries a and K_i1. Step 3: column elimination makes row 1 vanish because ab=1. Step 4: row elimination uses ba=1; L0 then scales row 1 by b to give a corner of 1, and the order is correct by associativity. Step 5: continuity uses only the topological-ring operations and the separate hypothesis that the pivot inverse is continuous. Step 6: empty blocks and empty T. Every step is honestly elementary. I ran my own test on 16200 random cases over Z/1, Z/4, Z/6, Z/8, Z/9 and Z/12 with shapes up to 3x3; all identities and both two-sided inverses hold. lean.statement: theorem continuous_unitPivot_schur_formula {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] {T : Type v} [TopologicalSpace T] {n m : ℕ} (K : T → Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) A) (hK : ∀ i j, Continuous (fun t => K t i j)) (hunit : ∀ t, IsUnit (K t 0 0)) (hinv : Continuous (fun t => Ring.inverse (K t 0 0))) : (∀ t, IsUnit (unitPivotLeft (K t))) ∧ (∀ t, IsUnit (unitPivotRightElimination (K t))) ∧ (∀ i j, Continuous (fun t => unitPivotLeft (K t) i j)) ∧ (∀ i j, Continuous (fun t => unitPivotRightElimination (K t) i j)) ∧ (∀ i j, Continuous (fun t => Ring.inverse (unitPivotLeft (K t)) i j)) ∧ (∀ i j, Continuous (fun t => Ring.inverse (unitPivotRightElimination (K t)) i j)) ∧ (∀ i j, Continuous (fun t => unitPivotSchurComplement (K t) i j)) ∧ (∀ t, unitPivotLeft (K t) * K t * unitPivotRightElimination (K t) = of (Fin.cases (Fin.cases 1 (fun _ => 0)) (fun i => Fin.cases 0 (unitPivotSchurComplement (K t) i))))
lean.note: Positive dimensions are n + 1 and m + 1. The five helper definitions are the prescribed factors and residual block of this node. IsUnit expresses membership in the general linear group, and Ring.inverse agrees with the inverse of each unit.

reviewed_lean.note: The Lean statement matches every hypothesis and conclusion of the node: arbitrary commutative topological ring, independent universes u and v, sizes n+1 and m+1, entrywise-continuous K, unit pivot with continuous Ring.inverse, L0, L1 and R0 as prescribed, L=L0*L1, H on the successor indices. The eight conjuncts give IsUnit, entry continuity of the matrices and their inverses, continuity of H, and L*K*R0 = diag(1,H) with the Fin.cases layout checked.
